headline: NBR makes online tax return submission mandatory for individuals
summary: Taxpayers can now file returns throughout the year, with a 5% rebate for early submissions between July 1 and September 30.
details: The National Revenue Board (NBR) has made the online submission of income tax returns mandatory for individual taxpayers in the new tax year.

Certain categories remain exempt, including foreign nationals working in Bangladesh, taxpayers aged 65 or above, physically challenged individuals, Bangladeshi taxpayers residing abroad, and legal representatives of dead taxpayers.
Manual returns are still permitted under specific circumstances, such as technical glitches or registration issues, subject to formal approval from authorities.
Under new proposals, tax returns can now be submitted throughout the year. Those who file early between July 1 and September 30 will receive a 5% rebate on their payable tax, capped at Tk 25,000.
Taxpayers filing in the second quarter (Oct 1 to Dec 31) will not receive a rebate but will not face additional tax burdens.
Late filings in the third quarter (Jan 1 to Mar 31) will incur a penalty of 2% of the tax amount or a maximum of Tk 3,000.
Returns submitted in the final quarter (Apr 1 to Jun 30) will incur a penalty of 5% of the tax amount or 3,000 to 5,000 Taka
Previously, individual taxpayers could file returns under standard procedures until November 30 without additional tax burdens.

headline_marked: Up to 142% hike: [[Govt employees may get full basic pay raise]] from July
headline: Up to 142% hike: Govt employees may get full basic pay raise from July
summary: The Ninth Pay Scale could be implemented in two phases, with basic salaries increasing first and allowances following in the next fiscal year.
details: The government may implement the Ninth Pay Scale in two phases, with the full increase in basic salaries likely to take effect from July and increased allowances to follow in the next fiscal year.

A secretaries’ committee is expected to submit its evaluation and implementation roadmap to the finance ministry this week, with a gazette notification expected by mid-July pending prime minister's approval.

The committee is expected to recommend a 100 percent or slightly lower increase in basic salaries for employees in grades 1 to 10, and an average increase of around 130 percent for those in grades 11 to 20.
The Ninth Pay Commission recommended basic salary increases ranging from 100 percent to 142 percent, along with substantial increases in other benefits.
The proposed budget for fiscal 2026-27 has earmarked Tk 44,000 crore for the partial implementation of the new pay structure.
Public servants have remained under the same pay structure for the past 11 years, despite a sharp rise in living costs due to inflation.
The government currently spends approximately Tk 1,31,000 crore annually on salaries and pensions for about 14 lakh employees and 9 lakh pensioners.
